_note: First slice: mid-1870s to mid-1880s drives and railheads. Run length is days; about 4400 days from 1874 reaches early 1886; the first year is warm-up while towns settle toward their trade income.
_leaders_note: Fictional men for hire who can raise and train a posse; skill multiplies posse strength.
_campaigns_note: Troop strength follows threats from outside the model, not local robberies. Dates and sizes approximate; verify.

campaigns.name: Red River War
campaigns.cause: Army campaign on the Southern Plains (Red River War, 1874-75) after conflict with the Kiowa, Comanche and Southern Cheyenne

campaigns.name: Great Sioux War
campaigns.cause: Army campaign on the Northern Plains after the Black Hills gold rush brought miners onto Lakota land

campaigns.name: Fort Keogh established
campaigns.cause: the Army garrisoned the Yellowstone country after the 1876 campaign, building a permanent post at the Tongue River

shocks.name: Black Hills gold rush
shocks.cause: Custer's 1874 expedition confirmed gold; the 1876 rush ignored the Fort Laramie treaty

shocks.name: Hard winter
shocks.cause: overstocked northern range and a severe winter (the 1886-87 die-out)
